explanation: Gelatin is broken-down collagen, extracted by heating animal tissue in water. Vegetarian versions often use agar, from red seaweed, while jam sets thanks to pectin, found in fruit.

claims.text: Gelatin is usually made from collagen extracted from animal skin, bones and connective tissue.
Gelatin is not made from red seaweed, citrus peel or cassava starch, which give agar, pectin and tapioca starch.
Gelatin is partly broken-down collagen, extracted by heating animal tissues in water.
Agar, a gelling agent made from red seaweed, is used in vegetarian alternatives to gelatin.
Jam sets because of pectin, found in fruit.
